questions.prompt: Why is two-phase commit across microservices rarely used?
options: Every participant needs the same protocol, locks are held while the slowest votes, and a coordinator failure strands them
A sequence of local transactions, each with a compensating transaction

questions.prompt: Charging the card succeeds, then booking a courier fails. What runs?
options: Refund the card, then release the items, in reverse order

questions.prompt: A compensation makes it as if the step never happened, like a database rollback.
Where should an irreversible step like sending a confirmation email go?
options: Last, after the saga can no longer fail

questions.prompt: The step after which a saga is guaranteed to complete is the ______. (one word)
Which saga style keeps the whole flow in one place?
Why do most teams orchestrate sagas of more than a few steps?
options: With choreography, nobody can see the whole flow without reading every service, and event cycles creep in
